$$

For any set $S,$ we have $|P(S)|={2}^{|S|}.$ Also, $|S\times T|=|S|\cdot |T|.$

In our case, 

$$
|A|=1,\,|B|=2.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}|P(A)| & ={2}^{|A|}={2}^{1}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|P(P(A))| & ={2}^{|P(A)|} \\  & ={2}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|P(P(A))\times B| & =|P(P(A))|\cdot |B| \\  & =4\cdot 2 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following sets are finite?

I. $P(\{R,e\})$

II. $P(\{x\in R∣\operatorname{cos}⁡x=0\})$

III. $P(\{(-1)^{n}∣n\in Z\})$
questions.worked_solution:
The power set of a finite set is finite, while the power set of an infinite set is infinite.

With that in mind, let's examine our sets.

- Set I is finite since the underlying set is finite. Notice that 

$$
P(\{R,e\})=\{∅,\,\{R\},\,\{e\},\,\{R,e\}\}
$$

has cardinality $4.$

- Set II is infinite since the underlying set $\{x\in R∣\operatorname{cos}⁡x=0\}$  is infinite.

- Set III is finite since the underlying set is finite. Notice that 

$$
\{(-1)^{n}∣n\in Z\}=\{-1,1\},
$$

and, as a result, 

$$
P(\{(-1)^{n}∣n\in Z\})=P(\{-1,1\})=\{∅,\,\{-1\},\,\{1\},\,\{-1,1\}\}
$$

has cardinality $4.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
